content:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for gateway-service in us-west-2 (p95/p99 latency spike). Auto-threshold triggered at 03/15 10:14 UTC. Link: https://monitoring.redwood/g/alerts/4523456789
alex: paging @oncall-sre and @jamal — seeing errors climbing fast, routing errors + timeouts reported by clients.
maria: noticed a deploy finished ~10:08 UTC (commit `feat/batching-optim`). Could be related.
jamal: confirmed — I saw a canary rollout at 10:07:54, small percentage. Telemetry shows tail latency jump around 10:09:30. p95 from 120ms -> 2.1s, p99 -> 8.4s. 5xx mostly 504/gateway-timeout and 502 from proxy.
emily: are errors concentrated to a subset of hosts or all AZs?
jamal: logs show higher queue wait on runtime nodes behind loadbalancer pool A (us-west-2a). Pool B less affected.
oncall-sre: I'm on it, watching dashboards. Assigning incident severity P1.
alex: product-ops please pull customer impact list, any active SLAs? @product-ops
product-ops: pulling list now. Tentative customers on Dedicated have increased errors; Hosted API shows degraded throughput for long prompt workloads.
incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4523456789. Paging rotation started: @oncall-sre primary, @jamal secondary.
jamal: quick tail trace snippet: ```
2026-03-15T10:09:31Z runtime-123 WARN kv_cache_miss wait_ms=2100 queue_len=128
2026-03-15T10:09:32Z proxy-45 ERROR upstream_timeout id=abcd status=504
```
alex: can we roll back the canary? If deploy is the culprit, rollback immediate to previous stable.
emily: before rollback, can we throttle long requests or apply a shorter timeout at gateway to prevent queue buildup? Might reduce cascade.
oncall-sre: quick mitigation: 1) increase bypass to pool B for new requests 2) temporarily reduce canary traffic to 0% 3) raise autoscale min for runtime group in us-west-2a by +20%
jamal: initiating canary pause via deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: Pausing rollout for `feat/batching-optim` (deploy id: d-2026-03-15-1007). Traffic percentage set to 0%.
alex: good. Also flip route for high-latency large-seq requests to experimental fallback model variant (lower memory). This reduces KV cache pressure.
maria: routing rule change pushed (rule id: r-998) — large-seq => model-quantized-v1 in fallback pool.
jamal: seeing immediate drop in queue_len metrics on pool A after route change, p95 improving but p99 still elevated for a subset.
oncall-sre: customer impact summary: approx 12% of requests in the last 5m saw 5xx/timeouts, mainly long sequence generation. No data plane errors (no data loss). Escalate to SEs for high-touch customers as precaution.
product-ops: drafting status note for affected customers, ETA for rollback decision in 6m if not stabilized.
emily: I still see backend errors tied to `kv_cache_eviction` logs — could be memory pressure introduced by batching change in the new build.
jamal: I recommend full rollback of the deploy artifact to previous stable; mitigations helped but not fully back to baseline.
alex: agree. Jamal, can you execute rollback and coordinate with SRE?
jamal: rolling back now — command: `deploy rollback d-2026-03-15-1007 --to d-2026-03-10-0912 --force`
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for deploy id d-2026-03-15-1007 -> target d-2026-03-10-0912. Estimated completion ~45s.
incidents-bot: Note: automated postmortem checklist created. Attach logs and traces to INC-2026-4523456789.
oncall-sre: rollback complete. Observability: p95 back to ~140ms within 90s of rollback, p99 trending down to ~250ms. 5xx rate dropping toward baseline.
alex: :thumbsup: Good. Keep monitoring for 10m, then start stabilization window. Jamal, can you file a blameless postmortem and include reproduction steps & telemetry?
jamal: will do. I'll include the failing code path, trace snippets, and memory/kv metrics.
maria: recommend disabling the aggressive batching flag until we test additional load scenarios.
emily: adding failing test to CI to catch queue-growth regressions.
product-ops: I posted a short customer update: "We experienced elevated timeouts and 5xx for long-running requests after a recent canary deploy; rollback completed and service is recovering. No data loss. We will follow up with postmortem."
oncall-sre: handoff: I'll remain on watch for 30m then pass to next oncall with notes. If metrics re-escalate, re-open pager.
alex: great work team — follow up actions: rollback postmortem, CI test, rollback gating for batching flags, and a runbook update for kv_cache pressure.
incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-4523456789 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Closing to P1 once stable for 30m.
product-ops: tagging customers and support threads, marking high-touch customers for outreach.
jamal: filing postmortem now: link will be attached to the incident.```
